name: MathlibAnnex.BilipschitzOrientation.targetJacobianSign_ae_const
title: Almost-everywhere constancy of the sign on a preconnected target

content.display_title: Almost-everywhere constancy of the sign on a preconnected target
content.one_sentence_role: Obtains one constant from the weak equation and preconnectedness of the target.
content.natural_language_statement:
Let $n\in\mathbb N_0$ and let $E=\mathbb R^n$ have the sup norm $\|\cdot\|_\infty$. Let $S,T\subseteq E$ be open, and let $f,g:E\to E$ be globally Lipschitz maps whose restrictions $f|_S:S\to T$ and $g|_T:T\to S$ are mutually inverse. Fix a number $\ell>0$ such that
$$\ell\|x-x'\|_\infty\le\|f(x)-f(x')\|_\infty\qquad(x,x'\in E).$$

The target $T$ is **preconnected**: it cannot be written as the union of two disjoint, nonempty, relatively open subsets. The empty set is allowed.

Write $Df(x):E\to E$ for the Fréchet derivative of $f$ at $x$ when it exists, and set $Df(x)=0$ at other points. Define the signed Jacobian by $J_f(x)=\det Df(x)$.

Define the source sign $s_f:E\to\{-1,1\}$ and its transport $\sigma_f:E\to\{-1,1\}$ by
$$s_f(x)=\begin{cases}1,&J_f(x)\ge0,\\-1,&J_f(x)<0,\end{cases}\qquad \sigma_f(y)=s_f(g(y)).$$
In particular, a zero determinant gives sign $+1$, and $|\sigma_f(y)|=1$ for every $y$.

Let $\lambda$ be Lebesgue measure on $E$. Then there exists $c\in\mathbb R$ such that
$$\lambda\bigl(\{y\in T:\sigma_f(y)\ne c\}\bigr)=0.$$
Equivalently, $\sigma_f(y)=c$ for Lebesgue-almost every $y\in T$.
content.assumptions:
The target $T$ is **preconnected**: it cannot be written as the union of two disjoint, nonempty, relatively open subsets. The empty set is allowed. This is an explicit hypothesis in addition to openness of $T$. No positive-measure or finite-measure hypothesis is imposed.

The sets $S,T\subseteq E$ are open. The inverse and image conditions are
$$\begin{aligned}
f(S)&\subseteq T,&g(T)&\subseteq S,\\
g(f(x))&=x\quad(x\in S),&f(g(y))&=y\quad(y\in T).
\end{aligned}$$
The global bounds use specified constants $C_f,C_g\ge0$ and $\ell>0$:
$$\ell\|x-x'\|_\infty\le\|f(x)-f(x')\|_\infty\le C_f\|x-x'\|_\infty\qquad(x,x'\in E),$$
$$\|g(y)-g(y')\|_\infty\le C_g\|y-y'\|_\infty\qquad(y,y'\in E).$$
The estimates hold on all of $E$, not just on $S$ or $T$. The inverse identities are required only on $S$ and $T$.
content.conclusion: A single real number $c$ agrees with the transported Jacobian sign outside a null subset of $T$. If $T=\varnothing$, every $c$ satisfies this equality; this declaration does not constrain that choice to $\{-1,1\}$ in the empty case.
content.proof_summary: The sign is locally integrable and satisfies the zero-weak-gradient equation. Apply the constancy theorem with domain $T$ and scalar function $\sigma_f$, using the explicit preconnectedness hypothesis.

proof_steps.text:
**Supply local integrability and the weak equation.** Since $|\sigma_f|=1$, every compact set $K\subseteq T$ satisfies
$$\int_K|\sigma_f(y)|\,d\lambda(y)=\lambda(K)<\infty.$$
The total derivative is measurable, the determinant and its two-valued sign are measurable, and $g$ is continuous. Thus $\sigma_f$ is measurable and locally integrable on $T$, as recorded by [local integrability of the transported sign](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Calculus/BilipschitzOrientation/Constancy.lean#L27-L48). The absolute-value equality is recorded by [the source-sign bound](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Calculus/BilipschitzOrientation/Basic.lean#L170-L174) and [the transported-sign bound](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Calculus/BilipschitzOrientation/Basic.lean#L176-L179).

For every $C^1$ vector field $W:E\to E$ that is zero outside a compact subset of $T$, write $\operatorname{div}W=\operatorname{tr}DW$. Then
$$\int_T\sigma_f(y)\operatorname{div}W(y)\,d\lambda(y)=0.$$
This is [the zero-weak-gradient theorem](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Calculus/BilipschitzOrientation/Piola.lean#L429-L446) for the same maps, target set and Lebesgue measure.

**Apply constancy on this target.** The hypotheses now read
$$T\text{ open and preconnected},\qquad \sigma_f\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(T,\lambda),\qquad \nabla\sigma_f=0\text{ weakly on }T.$$
Apply [the preconnected-domain constancy theorem](https://github.com/r-tanaka-math/mathlib-annex/blob/437e6e46228bbb8e91211ebded349d7a30020e73/MathlibAnnex/Analysis/Distribution/WeakGradient.lean#L21-L28) with ambient space $E=\mathbb R^n$, Lebesgue measure $\lambda$, open set $U=T$, and scalar function $u=\sigma_f$. Openness and preconnectedness are assumptions; Step 1 supplies local integrability and the weak equation. Its output is
$$\exists c\in\mathbb R:\quad\lambda\bigl(\{y\in T:\sigma_f(y)\ne c\}\bigr)=0,$$
which is exactly the asserted conclusion. This application allows both $n=0$ and $T=\varnothing$.

content.lean_realization_notes: The pointwise bound $|\sigma_f|=1$ supplies local integrability even if $T$ has infinite measure. When $T$ has positive measure, a chosen almost-everywhere constant can be identified with an actual sign value.
